podcast.body: Released from their first album, this single did "quite well" in the US initially, but the label then decided not to release another single, which the band views as the start of their difficulties in America. "And in the States, we released Tri-Honesty and it did quite well and then the label had a choice to release another single and they didn't."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Billy Talent In Their Own Words: Part 2

podcast.body: This song was an early release on a 2001 demo CD, the "Billy Talent EP," and was crucial for the band's development. Ian D'Sa started working on this song in Montreal, and it became a catalyst for a new era of the band when he returned and presented it. "This is an early release of Try Honesty. And it's with this recording that the Billy Talent sound starts to come through."
